what: What did each Lunenburg town employee earn in 1992?
why: `report-gross-wages` holds per-employee earnings from the 2010 report (calendar wages) and FY2011-FY2025 (fiscal). The 1992 annual town report prints no wage list: its text was searched for wage, gross, earning, payroll, compensation and employee on every page (64 of 64 have text) and returned only prose in department reports (p6, p9, p31), the balance-sheet line EMPLOYEES' WITHHOLD PAYABLE (p23), the receipts line EARNINGS ON INVESTMENTS (p24), department lines in the appropriations schedule (p26, p28) and the FY1993 budget vote (p47), and warrant-article prose (p46, p52) -- no list by employee (sources/data/report-tables/1992/). — closes: the Town's calendar-1992 payroll register (W-2 totals by employee) from the Treasurer's office.

what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates in 1992?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1992 annual town report prints neither: its text was searched for salary schedule, classification, step and grade on every page and returned only school grade levels (p15-p22) and one mention of the `Salary Administration Plan` in a special town meeting article (p52), with no schedule (sources/data/report-tables/1992/). — closes: the Salary Administration Plan schedule (grades and steps) in force for FY1993, from the Town Clerk or the Personnel Board.

what: What did each item of Lunenburg's FY1993 capital plan cost, and what was left in each capital project fund at 30 June 1992?
why: `capital-plans` and `report-capital-projects` hold these from the 2010 report and 2001. The 1992 annual town report prints neither a capital plan nor a capital project fund schedule: its text was searched for capital on every page and returned only the index entry `Capital Planning Committee` (p2), with no such report printed, and the fire chief's prose (p8). Capital items were voted one article at a time in the April 11, 1992 town meeting excerpts, in prose with an amount each (p48-p51, e.g. `VOTED UNANIMOUSLY TO RAISE $13,330 BY BORROWING`), and the bonds authorized and unissued at 30 June 1992 are listed on p33 (sources/data/report-tables/1992/). — closes: the Capital Planning Committee's FY1993 report and the Town Accountant's capital project fund ledger at 30 June 1992.

what: What was Lunenburg's FY1992 tax levy and assessed value by property class, with its overlay and new growth?
why: `report-valuation` holds the Assessors' tables (assessments and revenues by class, abstract by class code, overlay, new growth) from the 2010 report and 2001. The 1992 annual town report prints no Assessors' table: its text was searched for assessed, valuation, tax rate, levy, overlay, abatement, exemption and new growth on every page and returned only two valuation figures and a tax rate in prose on the About the Town page (p3: `ASSESSED VALUATION: - $481,456,703-Real Estate - $12,165,184-Personal Prop. TAX RATE: $14.43 (Fiscal 1993)`, the valuation's year not printed), the Assessors' prose report (p6-p7), and abatement lines in the balance sheet, receipts and collection of taxes (p23, p24, p34) (sources/data/report-tables/1992/). — closes: the FY1992 and FY1993 tax rate recapitulation (Form RECAP) and LA-4 as filed with the Division of Local Services.

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1992, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and fees from the 2010 report. The 1992 annual town report prints no Inspector of Weights & Measures report: its text was searched for weights, sealer and sealing and returned only the index entry (p2), the appointment (p5), the receipts line SEALING FEES $669.00 (p24), the appropriation line Inspector Weights & Measures $1,070.00 (p26) and the FY1993 budget line INSPECTOR OF WEIGHTS & MEASURES 1,070 (p47) (sources/data/report-tables/1992/). — closes: the Sealer of Weights and Measures' 1992 annual report to the Division of Standards.

what: How much of Lunenburg's debt at 30 June 1992 sat inside the debt limit, and how much outside it?
why: `outstanding-debt` reads this from the five-year outstanding-debt summary the FY2011-FY2025 reports print. The 1992 annual town report prints its bonded indebtedness issue by issue (p33) and a repayment schedule (p35-p36) whose interest lines are marked `INTEREST (EXEMPTED)` for some issues, but no summary by purpose and no debt-limit split: its text was searched for debt limit, outstanding debt and indebtedness and returned only the index and the two page headings (sources/data/report-tables/1992/). — closes: the Town's FY1992 Statement of Indebtedness as filed with the Division of Local Services.
